title: Asparagus, frozen, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Asparagus is the edible shoot of the plant Asparagus officinalis. Frozen asparagus cooked with butter or margarine is a ready‑to‑eat product that retains most of its nutrients and its characteristic tender flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Asparagus is one of the oldest cultivated vegetables, grown for over 2,000 years.
Freezing preserves its bright green color and crisp texture.
Cooking with butter or margarine enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin K.
Asparagus contains aromatic compounds that become more pronounced with a light sauté in butter.
In the United States, frozen cooked asparagus is often sold as a convenient side dish.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate supports DNA synthesis and is especially important during pregnancy.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: A serving provides few calories, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Asparagus supplies vitamin C, glutathione, and other antioxidants that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes digestive health and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to asparagus.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Asparagus contains oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Cooking with butter or margarine adds calories and fat; those monitoring fat intake should consider portion size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the frozen asparagus in a skillet or microwave, adding a pat of butter or margarine. Serve as a side dish with meat, fish, or incorporate into salads. Season with garlic, lemon juice, or your favorite herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen product in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F). Once thawed, use within 1–2 days and do not re‑freeze; discard if it develops an off odor or texture.
